Let the inputs $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit integers
Fix a digit width $b$, the number of bits in each radix digit,
let $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of radix digits of each input.
Here $x_j$ is the $j$th radix digit of $x$
and $y_j$ is the $j$th radix digit of $y$
where $c_k$ is the sum of $x_i\,y_j$ over all $0\le i,j\le q-1$ with $i+j=k$
here $h_k$ is the carry into position $k$
and $d_k$ is the output digit at position $k$.

gaps.quote: Each $c_k$ is at most $q(2^b-1)^2$, which is below $2^{3b}$ (cited).
gaps.note: The cited inequality is stated without the condition under which it holds (it needs q to be at most about 2^b, which the page never states), and the page never says why the bound is needed or where it is used later. The reader cannot check why the cited claim applies here or what role it plays.

The page asserts that the carries eventually vanish, which is needed to make the final equality xy = sum_k d_k 2^{bk} a finite identity, but gives no reason. The reader would have to supply the argument that c_k = 0 beyond index 2q-2 and that the carry recurrence then shrinks the carry to zero.
